question.text: Under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR), the Indian tax authorities have powers which are relevant to AIF structuring. Which of the following describes GAAR's most relevant implication for AIF structures?

answer.text: GAAR allows authorities to re-characterise transactions on grounds of lack of commercial substance
GAAR prohibits the use of any offshore pooling jurisdiction for Indian AIFs
GAAR mandates that every AIF pool must be constituted only as a trust
GAAR is applicable only to listed companies and has no bearing on AIF structures

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 132, complex structures may be scrutinised under GAAR and re-characterised for lack of commercial substance; per page 481, GAAR gives the tax authorities re-characterisation powers; per page 140, substance-over-form considerations influence offshore fund structures. The Trap: Option B over-states GAAR — it does not blanket-ban offshore pooling. Option C confuses GAAR with SEBI structural choice. Option D is false; GAAR is not limited to listed companies and can apply to AIF structures. Note: GAAR's relevance for AIF structuring lies in the substance-over-form test and the authorities' power to re-characterise transactions that lack commercial substance.
